planning_policy.basis: The null option. Costs nothing and changes nothing, which is exactly why it has to be scored alongside the rest rather than assumed away.
Affirming the current plan. Distinct from do_nothing only in that it is a recorded decision rather than an absence of one.
A few minutes of dispatcher and driver time. A phone call does not cool anything; its worth is the information it produces, which this model does not price.
A roadside stop and a look at the unit. Occasionally finds a resettable fault; against a degrading compressor it changes nothing on its own. Its value is diagnostic.
A flag for later. Changes nothing about this shipment, which is why its risk multiplier is 1.0 rather than a small discount.
Diverting to a cold-storage facility: fuel, driver hours, storage fees and a missed delivery window. The most effective intervention available and the most expensive.
Delivering to an alternative site. Cheaper than cold storage and less effective: it shortens the exposure rather than ending it.
Two vehicles out of service and a cargo transfer. Thorough, expensive, and it exposes the load during the transfer, which a fixed cold store does not.
Engineering attention to the reefer unit. Addresses the cause rather than the cargo, so it helps this shipment only if it arrives in time.
Tells the customer; does not change the cargo temperature. Its value is contractual and reputational, neither of which this expected-value model prices - see `decision.engine`.

llm_showcase.narrative: The cargo is currently 7.15 C inside a refrigerated unit that has a permitted maximum of 8.00 C, but the system estimates a 0.62 probability that the temperature will breach that envelope.  The compressor is running at 1488 RPM, a drop from 1779.60 RPM in 30 minutes, and a fault code [AL17] has been recorded, pointing to potential compressor degradation.  With a remaining 173 minutes to destination and a 35‑minute route delay, the risk of damage is high.  The recommended action is to reroute the vehicle to cold storage, costing 1800 USD and adding 180 minutes of delay, which offers the highest expected value.

lines.text: claim: temperature_within_envelope within 90 minutes
verdict: failed - 3 of the last 3 readings are outside [2.0, 8.0] C
incident reopened: investigating

Graded against the recording, which is the trajectory of a truck that was NOT rerouted: IncidentForge does not yet simulate post-action physics. So a failure here is the honest result, and it shows the reopen path against real readings. Synthesising a recovery to make the demo end happily would be fabricating an observation, which is the one thing the system refuses to do anywhere else.
